correctness.rationale: Cuts C subset [N], N=n-1, encode exactly all interval-block equivalences; a queried pair (i,j) is equal iff C avoids [i,j-1]. A pattern isolating one negative label forces a private cut site for that interval, and selecting exactly the private sites of negative labels realizes any pattern, proving iff. A valid family of intervals can be ordered by both endpoints with no nesting or triple overlap; a three-state A/B/D scan counts its starts, with matrix T=[[1,z,0],[1,1+z,z],[0,1,1]]. Its resolvent gives (1-2t+(1-z)t^2)/((1-t)(1-(2+z)t+(1-z)t^2)); coefficient extraction gives sum_j C(k-1,j)C(N+k-j,2k). Every interval requires one unique private site, giving VC<=N with equality only for N singleton intervals. Substituting z=1 yields known (3^N+1)/2 totals. One full interval is inclusion-maximal of size one while the adjacent support has size N, proving nonpurity. Independent complete cut-labelling tests for N=1..4 give polynomials 1+z; 1+3z+z^2; 1+6z+6z^2+z^3; 1+10z+20z^2+9z^3+z^4.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks are bounded; unrestricted assertions rest on the reconstructed combinatorial proof.
